title: Genesis Primitives that fire once permanently close their own invocation path rather than remaining dormant
content:
Across the Genesis Primitives in Launch Agent 7's Artifact, the In Progress Invocations directories carry an identical closure statement rather than a list. A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.1.4 and A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.4: "Because the Agent Creation Primitive is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked." A.6.1.1.8.2.1.2.1.4 says the same for Prime Transformation; A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.1.4 for the Agent Token Primitive ("Invoked solely for the one-time deployment of the Agent's token").

The design choice is to make single-use primitives *self-sealing*. A dormant-but-invocable primitive would leave a standing path to re-create the Agent or re-deploy its token; the Artifact instead records that the path no longer exists.

This is why the same primitives also declare no post-deployment operational process (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.3.1.2, A.6.1.1.8.2.1.2.3.1.2): if a primitive can never be invoked again, there is nothing left to operate. Genesis Primitives are therefore structurally different from ongoing operational primitives — they are one-shot constructors whose only lasting output is the configuration they wrote.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation and Agent Token each declare that no further Instances can ever be Invoked — the primitive is spent, not merely idle, so the one-time event cannot recur.
